title: Talk With Family and Friends
whyMatters: Family and friend reactions can shape your early experience as a Muslim. A calm plan helps you share wisely, protect safety, and avoid turning every conversation into a debate.

exactActions.text: Decide who needs to know now
subSteps: You do not need to tell everyone at the same time.
Prioritize people who affect your safety, housing, food, schedule, or emotional support.
If someone may react harshly, prepare with a mentor first.
Share what Islam means to you, not a long argument.
Let your character show the change over time.
They may fear you are becoming a different person.
They may have media-based misconceptions about Islam.
Answer gently and say when you do not know yet.
Pause conversations that become insulting or unsafe.
Stay connected where possible through kindness and service.
Ask for support if family pressure becomes controlling or threatening.

timeEstimate: Plan for 30 minutes before important conversations

obstacles.problem: My family thinks I rejected them
obstacles.solution: Reassure them through consistent kindness. You can explain that Islam deepens your commitment to good character and family ties.
You can say you are still learning and would rather keep the relationship peaceful. You do not have to answer every question immediately.

tinyVersion: Choose one safe person and prepare one calm sentence about why Islam matters to you.
unlocksNext: Healthy family boundaries make community, learning, and daily practice easier to sustain.

contextNotes.title: Safety first
contextNotes.body: If telling someone could risk housing, harm, or coercive control, speak with a trusted local support person before disclosing.

gentleScripts.title: First conversation
gentleScripts.body: I want to share something important with you. I became Muslim because I believe in one God and this path has brought me meaning. I am still learning, and I hope we can talk with respect.

gentleScripts.title: When a talk becomes heated
gentleScripts.body: I love you and I do not want this to become an argument. Can we pause and come back to it another time?
